title: Order No. 202-26-41, Federal Power Act Section 202(c): PJM Interconnection
date_evidence: Issued in Washington, D.C. on this 1st day of September 2026.
key_claim: DOE's 1 September 2026 order lets PJM direct backup generation at large loads as a last resort before or during an EEA 3, says emissions and operating hours will not be counted toward rolling limits while it is in force, and records PJM's expectation of exceedances of permit restrictions.
frame_summary: DOE treats backup generation as a last-resort grid resource and makes it usable by suspending, for the life of the order, the permit limits that otherwise bind it.
verbatim_quote: may result in exceedance of permit restrictions on sulfur dioxide, nitrogen oxide
verbatim_list: will not be counted toward applicable rolling average
to operate as a last resort before declaring an EEA 3 (i.e., before firm load interruption) or during an EEA 3
notes: WebFetch of the DOE order 20/10/2026; sandbox egress blocked for the audit scripts, quotes confirmed by hand against the live page text. Page extraction drops the hyphen in 'average-based', so the quote stops before it.

title: 202(c) Update in Preparation for Winter Season (Operating Committee)
key_claim: PJM's list of 2026 DOE orders shows five that authorise it to direct backup generation (26 January, 30 June, 14 July, 21 August, 1 September), four of them running seven days; it says PJM makes daily determinations of reliability need and lists Michigan v. DOE among its items.
frame_summary: PJM presents backup-generation orders as a recurring operating tool whose use it judges daily, and flags a court ruling on 202(c) as something it is assessing.
verbatim_quote: PJM will make daily determinations on the reliability need and applicability of the 202(c) order.
verbatim_list: Authorizing PJM to direct backup generation resources as a last resort before declaring an EEA 3
Refer to Manual 13: Attachment O for guidance on Emergency Use of Back-up Generation
notes: WebFetch 20/10/2026. The deck's Feb. 23 entry (Order 202-26-17) concerns Eddystone, not backup generation, and is not counted. Order lengths are taken from the 'through' dates on each entry (Jan 26 to Feb 2, Jun 30 to Jul 7, Jul 14 to Jul 21, Sep 1 to Sep 8; Aug 21 to Sep 18).

title: Manual 13 Revision 98 (Operating Committee presentation)
key_claim: Attachment O to PJM's Manual 13 is in effect only if PJM requests and DOE grants a Section 202(c) order; affected load must move to backup generation within 15 minutes; use under the order does not count toward annual run-hour limits.
frame_summary: PJM builds the backup-generation procedure as a conditional step that depends entirely on a federal emergency order and on exempting the engines from run-hour limits.
verbatim_quote: is only in effect if PJM requests, and the Department of Energy grants, a Section 202(c) order
verbatim_list: affected load must operate on back up generation within 15 minutes to avoid residential load shed
Allows backup generation at data centers to operate without counting toward annual run-hour limits
notes: WebFetch 20/10/2026. Structural anchor (141 days before scan date): canonical text of the procedure. Slide titled with 'OC Special Session', dated June 1, 2026.

title: Data Center Air Quality Permitting (presentation, 31 July 2026)
key_claim: Oregon DEQ lists grid dispatch as 'Currently not permitted at most data centers'; the state has 2,482 large data-centre generators with 6,328 MW of capacity; non-emergency operation is limited to 100 hours a year.
frame_summary: A state air regulator describes the permit baseline: emergency running is lightly regulated, but running engines to support the grid is outside most permits and capped in hours where allowed.
verbatim_quote: Currently not permitted at most data centers
notes: WebFetch 20/10/2026 of the slide deck by DEQ's Regional Air Quality Manager, hosted on the Oregon Department of Energy site. Oregon is outside PJM; used only as an illustration of a state permit baseline.

title: Federal appeals court vacates first DOE order on J.H. Campbell coal plant
key_claim: A federal appeals court ruled DOE's first order keeping the J.H. Campbell coal plant open was an unlawful use of Section 202(c); DOE has extended that order five times.
frame_summary: A state attorney general reports the first appellate ruling against DOE's use of emergency power under 202(c), on a coal-plant order rather than a backup-generation order.
verbatim_list: DOE has extended its order on five separate occasions.
notes: WebFetch 20/10/2026. A party's press release (Michigan was a petitioner); the ruling concerns a coal-plant order, not backup generation, and the article says so.

title: Report on health risks as federal agencies weaken pollution protections for data centres
key_claim: The network of former EPA officials documents at least 30 federal actions since January 2025 that raise pollution-related health risks as data centres expand; 17 of them explicitly cite or target AI or data centres.
frame_summary: Former regulators argue that federal environmental protections are being weakened specifically around data centres, which is the direction that would loosen permit limits.
verbatim_quote: Seventeen of the 30 actions documented by EPN explicitly cite or target AI or data centers.
verbatim_list: documents at least 30 federal actions since January 2025 that, taken together, increase pollution-related health risks
notes: WebFetch 20/10/2026. Advocacy-leaning nonprofit of former officials; the underlying health study is by UC Riverside, Caltech and RIT researchers. Used as directional evidence of policy direction, not for backup-generator numbers.

title: PJM Issued First Backup-Generator Warnings During Heat Wave
key_claim: PJM issued backup-generator warnings on 2 and 3 July but never escalated to an Action; it declined to disclose the total megawatts available; PJM's market monitor said the reserve's reliability contribution is not well known and PJM was close to a shortage of primary reserves.
frame_summary: Trade press reports that the backup-generator procedure was exercised for the first time as a warning only, with no published size for the resource.
verbatim_quote: actual extent of potential reliability contribution is not well known
verbatim_list: PJM declined to disclose the total megawatts available.
The significance is that PJM was getting very close to a shortage of primary reserves.
notes: WebFetch 20/10/2026; date is plain text with no datePublished markup. 92 days before scan date, at the edge of the 0-3m band.

title: PJM Market Monitor Says 42% Of Forecast Data Center Growth Is Delayed Or Canceled
key_claim: PJM's market monitor counted 4,016.9 MW of data-centre load canceled or delayed as of 21 September, 42% of PJM's forecast growth between 2026/27 and 2028/29; removing it cuts a 6,831.3 MW capacity gap to 3,055.0 MW.
frame_summary: Forbes reports the market monitor's argument that PJM's load forecast overstates data-centre growth, which would shrink the capacity shortfall that backup generation is meant to cover.
verbatim_quote: That is 42% of the growth in data center demand PJM had forecast between the 2026/27 and 2028/29 delivery years.
verbatim_list: Take the canceled and delayed load out and the 6,831.3 MW gap shrinks to 3,055.0 MW, a cut of 55%.
said 4,016.9 MW of data center load had been canceled or delayed as of Sept. 21.
notes: WebFetch 20/10/2026; page carries meta article:published 2026-10-12. The monitor is an interested party (it has asked FERC to reject PJM's filing) and its count comes from a commercial tracker; the article says so.
